extracted.intended_audience: auditors of Federal awards (OMB A-133 single audits), pass-through entity grant administrators and recipient financial/program staff
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for planning and performing compliance tests for Federal awards under OMB Circular A-133, covering procurement, program income, real property acquisition and relocation, reporting, subrecipient monitoring, special tests, and Student Financial Assistance cluster requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justification for limiting competition
rubrics_metrics.description: Examine documentation in support of the rationale to limit competition in those cases where competition was limited and ascertain if the limitation was justified (§ .36(b)(1) and (d)(4); and § .43 and § -44(e)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inspect procurement files to ensure the stated reasons for noncompetitive procurements are documented and consistent with cited regulations. Consider whether the limitation aligns with statutory/regulatory exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost or price analysis documented and supporting procurement actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Verify that contract files exist and ascertain if appropriate cost or price analysis was performed in connection with procurement actions, including contract modifications and that this analysis supported the procurement action (§ .36(f) and § .45).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test that analyses are present, complete, and demonstrate reasonableness of prices including justification for modifications; trace to procurement decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal awarding agency approval for certain procurements over $100,000
rubrics_metrics.description: Verify that the awarding Federal agency approved procurements exceeding $100,000 when such approval was required. Procurements (1) awarded by noncompetitive negotiation, (2) awarded when only a single bid or offer was received, (3) awarded to other than the apparent low bidder, or (4) specifying a 'brand name' product (§ .36(g)(1) and § -44(e)), may require prior Federal awarding agency approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check for documented prior approvals from the Federal awarding agency where these procurement circumstances occur; absence of approval is noncompliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with award-specific procurement requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Verify compliance with other procurement requirements specific to an award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review the terms and conditions of each award to identify and test program-specific procurement requirements; Procedure 5 applies to States and Federal awards subgranted by the State to a local government or Indian tribal government.

rubrics_metrics.name: State law and procedure adherence in procurements (Procedure 5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Test a sample of procurements to ascertain if the State's laws and procedures were followed and that the policies and procedures used were the same as for State funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For State-administered programs, ensure procurements conform to applicable State statutes and that Federal funds were procured under the same policies as State funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension and debarment certifications or excluded parties checks
rubrics_metrics.description: Test a sample of procurements and subawards and ascertain if the required suspension and debarment certifications were received for subawards and covered contracts, or alternatively test against the GSA List of Parties Excluded From Federal Procurement or Nonprocurement Programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify required certifications are on file or that awardees were not on the GSA excluded parties list at time of award; document procedures used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of program income
rubrics_metrics.description: Program income is gross income received that is directly generated by the Federally-funded project during the grant period. Program income includes, but is not limited to, income from fees for services performed, use or rental of property acquired with grant funds, sale of commodities fabricated under a grant, and payments of principal and interest on loans made with grant funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this definition to identify potential program income sources; exclude items specifically listed as not program income (e.g., interest on grant funds covered under Cash Management).

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted uses/methods for program income and default rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Program income may be used in one of three methods; deducted from outlays, added to the project budget, or used to meet matching requirements. Unless specified otherwise by agency regulations or award terms, program income shall be deducted from program outlays. For R&D activities by colleges/universities and other nonprofits, the default method is to add program income to the project budget.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine applicable agency/award instructions to establish which method applies; apply defaults only where authorized and document the method used in accounting records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation for program income after grant period
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless Federal awarding agency regulations or the terms and conditions of the award specify otherwise, non-Federal entities have no obligation to the Federal Government regarding program income earned after the end of the grant period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider award language to determine obligations for post-period program income; do not assume ongoing obligations absent explicit provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program income audit objective
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether program income is correctly determined, recorded, and used in accordance with the program requirements, A-102 Common Rule, and OMB Circular A-110, as applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Audit should assess identification, measurement, recording, and authorized use of program income against laws, regulations, and award terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify program income (audit procedure)
rubrics_metrics.description: Review the laws, regulations, and the provisions of contract or grant agreements applicable to the program and ascertain if program income was anticipated. Ascertain requirements for determining or assessing the amount of program income (e.g., fee scales, prohibited fees), and requirements for recording and using program income.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Begin with documentation review to establish expectations and required methodologies for program income measurement and treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inquire and review accounting records for program income receipt
rubrics_metrics.description: Inquire of management and review accounting records to ascertain if program income was received.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform inquiries and ledger walkthroughs to locate receipts that meet the program income definition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determining/assessing program income — tests of calculations
rubrics_metrics.description: Perform tests to verify that program income was properly determined or calculated in accordance with stated criteria, and that program income was only collected from allowable sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recompute fee scales and other calculations; test eligibility of sources of income to confirm allowance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recording of program income — tests of accounting entries
rubrics_metrics.description: Perform tests to verify that all program income was properly recorded in the accounting records.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trace identified program income to accounting records and ensure classification and ledgers reflect correct treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of program income — tests of authorized application
rubrics_metrics.description: Perform tests to ascertain if program income was used in accordance with the program requirements, the A-102 Common Rule, and OMB Circular A-110.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify expenditures or offsets funded by program income comply with the method authorized for the award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Real property appraisal process and review appraisal documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Test records to ascertain if (1) the just compensation amount offered the property owner was determined by an appraisal process; (2) the appraisal(s) was examined by a review appraiser; and (3) the review appraiser prepared a signed statement which explains the basis for adjusting comparable sales to reach the review appraiser's determination of the fair market value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine appraisals, review appraiser reports, and signed statements to ensure independent valuation and documented adjustments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written offer and justification for purchase price above appraised value
rubrics_metrics.description: Test supporting documentation to ascertain if (1) a written offer of the appraised value was made to the property owner, and (2) a written justification was prepared if the purchase price for the property exceeded the amount offered and that the documentation (e.g., recent court awards, estimated trial costs, valuation problems) supports such administrative settlement as being reasonable, prudent, and in the public interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify offers were made and any settlements above appraisal are supported by contemporaneous written justification and appropriate evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision of comparable replacement dwellings for residential relocations
rubrics_metrics.description: Test supporting documentation to ascertain if the non-Federal entity made available to the displaced persons one or more comparable replacement dwellings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm searches and availability analyses were documented and dwellings offered meet comparability criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replacement housing payments — occupancy and comparable dwelling analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: For a sample, test records to ascertain: (a) owner occupied the displacement dwelling for at least 180 days immediately prior to initiation of negotiations; (b) the non-Federal entity examined at least three comparable replacement dwellings available for sale and computed the payment based on the price of the dwelling most representative of the displacement dwelling; (c) asking price adjusted as justified by local market data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify occupancy history, comparable dwelling selection, and market adjustments are documented and calculations traceable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replacement housing payments — buy-down computation and last resort justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Allowance for increased mortgage cost buy-down amount was computed based on remaining principal balance, interest rate, and remaining term of the old mortgage; non-Federal entity prepared written justification on the need to employ last resort housing provisions if the total replacement housing payment exceeded $22,500.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recompute buy-downs and ensure threshold-based justifications (>$22,500) are present and support use of last resort provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rental or downpayment assistance documentation and occupancy timing
rubrics_metrics.description: For a sample, test records to ascertain: (a) the displacee occupied the displacement dwelling for at least 90 days immediately prior to initiation of negotiations; (b) the displacee rented or purchased and occupied a decent, safe, and sanitary replacement dwelling within one year; (c) written justification prepared if the payment exceeded $5,250.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check occupancy proofs, replacement dwelling condition, timelines, and written justifications when payments exceed thresholds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Business relocation moving expenses and reestablishment payments controls
rubrics_metrics.description: For a sample of business relocations: (a) verify payments for moving and related expenses were for actual costs incurred or fixed payments were limited to a maximum of $20,000 and computed based on average annual net earnings evidenced by tax returns or certified financials; (b) verify business reestablishment expense eligibility and that payments were for actual costs incurred and did not exceed $10,000.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review documentation of costs, methods for computing fixed payments, and eligibility evidence for reestablishment assistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of standard financial reporting forms and prescribed accounting basis
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients should use the standard financial reporting forms or such other forms as may be authorized by OMB. Each recipient must report program outlays and program income on a cash or accrual basis, as prescribed by the Federal awarding agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm recipients use the correct forms (FSR SF-269/SF-269A, SF-270, SF-271, SF-272) and the reporting accounting basis matches award instructions; if accrual information is required but books are cash-basis, verify analytical conversions are performed.

rubrics_metrics.name: PMS (Payment Management System) reporting verification
rubrics_metrics.description: For recipients using PMS, auditors should ensure amounts provided by agencies and DPM are in agreement with the recipient's records and are otherwise accurate. Perform steps to verify PMS 272, 272-A, 272-B, and 272-E as they pertain to the PMS reports regardless of data source.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare authorization amounts, drawdowns, collections, and disbursements between PMS reports and recipient records; annotate/trace resolutions for discrepancies and review PMS 272-A submissions and corrections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance reporting frequency and content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients shall submit performance reports at least annually but not more frequently than quarterly. Performance reports generally contain: (1) a comparison of actual accomplishments with goals and objectives for the period; (2) reasons why established goals were not met, if appropriate; (3) other pertinent information including analysis of cost overruns or high unit costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify timeliness and that reports include the required comparisons, explanations, and pertinent analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for testing performance and special reporting data
rubrics_metrics.description: Compliance testing of performance and special reporting is only required for data that are quantifiable and meet the following criteria: (1) have a direct and material effect on the program; (2) are capable of evaluation against objective criteria stated in the laws, regulations, contract or grant agreements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select performance metrics that meet these criteria for substantive testing; exclude non-quantifiable narrative items from compliance testing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analytical procedures for reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Perform appropriate analytical procedures and ascertain the reason for any unexpected differences (e.g., comparing current period reports to prior period reports; comparing anticipated results to reported data; comparing audit financial statement information to the reports).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use analytical results to shape nature, timing, and extent of further tests of reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sampling and testing of financial, performance, and special reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Select a sample of report types and: (a) for financial reports, ascertain preparation on required accounting basis, trace amounts to accounting records and schedules, verify agreement with accounting records and resolution of PMS discrepancies; (b) for performance/special reports, trace data to underlying records, perform tests of underlying data, and verify intervening computations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trace and recompute reported elements, verify links between worksheets and reports, and test mathematical accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completeness testing of reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Test selected reports for completeness: (a) for financial reports, review accounting records and ascertain if all applicable accounts were included (e.g., program income, loans, interest); (b) for performance/special reports, review supporting records to ascertain if all applicable data elements were included.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure that omitted items are identified and that reports represent all reportable activity for the period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Management written representation on reports provided
rubrics_metrics.description: Obtain written representation from management that the reports provided to the auditor are true copies of the reports submitted or electronically transmitted to the Federal awarding agency, DPM for PMS users, or pass-through entity in the case of a subrecipient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Secure signed management representation to corroborate that auditor-reviewed reports match those the recipient submitted to agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pass-through entity responsibility to identify award information and compliance requirements to subrecipients
rubrics_metrics.description: A pass-through entity is responsible for identifying to the subrecipient the Federal award information (e.g., CFDA title and number, award name, name of Federal agency) and applicable compliance requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify award documents and agreements notify subrecipients of award identifiers and applicable compliance areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring subrecipient activities to provide reasonable assurance of compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: A pass-through entity must monitor the subrecipient's activities to provide reasonable assurance that the subrecipient administers Federal awards in compliance with Federal requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess monitoring frequency and procedures (report review, site visits, agreed-upon procedures, audit reviews) for adequacy given award size/complexity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure required audits and corrective action by subrecipients
rubrics_metrics.description: Pass-through entities must ensure required audits are performed and require the subrecipient to take prompt corrective action on any audit findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm pass-through obtains subrecipient audit reports, issues timely management decisions, and tracks corrective action implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate impact of subrecipient activities on pass-through entity compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate the impact of subrecipient activities on the pass-through entity's ability to comply with applicable Federal regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider award concentration, dollar amounts, and identified deficiencies when assessing pass-through risk exposure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factors influencing extent of subrecipient monitoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Factors such as the size of awards, percentage of the total program's funds awarded to subrecipients, and the complexity of the compliance requirements may influence the extent of monitoring procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tailor monitoring intensity based on these risk factors; document rationale for monitoring scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forms of subrecipient monitoring activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Monitoring activities may include reviewing reports submitted by subrecipients, performing site visits to review records and observe operations, arranging agreed-upon procedures engagements, reviewing subrecipient single audits or program-specific audits, and evaluating corrective action plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select a mix of monitoring techniques appropriate to the risk and complexity of subrecipient activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require audits for subrecipients expending $300,000 or more
rubrics_metrics.description: Verify that the pass-through entity required subrecipients expending $300,000 or more in Federal awards during the subrecipient's fiscal year to have audits made in accordance with OMB Circular A-133.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test award agreements and monitoring records to ensure the threshold-triggered audit requirement was enforced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audit procedures to verify subrecipient monitoring practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Discuss subrecipient monitoring with pass-through staff to understand scope; test award documents to ascertain notification of award info and allowable activities; review monitoring documentation to verify monitoring and responses; verify receipt of subrecipient audit reports and timely management decisions; verify effects of subrecipient noncompliance are reflected in pass-through records.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate testing with other compliance areas (cash management, eligibility, procurement) to avoid duplication and to comprehensively test subrecipient oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify and test Special Tests and Provisions unique to each program
rubrics_metrics.description: The specific requirements for Special Tests and Provisions are unique to each Federal program and are found in the laws, regulations, and the provisions of contract or grant agreements. Auditor shall review contract and grant agreements and referenced laws to identify the compliance requirements and develop audit objectives and procedures for Special Tests and Provisions which could have a direct and material effect on a major program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For programs included in this Supplement, follow Part 4 or Part 5 provisions; for other programs, auditor must identify program-specific tests and include any additional material compliance requirements, including those arising from prior audit resolutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify additional non-law compliance requirements (audit resolution obligations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify any additional compliance requirements which are not based in law or regulation (e.g., were agreed to as part of audit resolution of prior audit findings) which could be material to a major program, and include them in the audit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inquire of management and review contracts/grant agreements to find such obligations and plan reasonable procedures to test compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of Y2K (major system-date) risks when relevant
rubrics_metrics.description: Although the auditor is not expected to plan and perform procedures to determine whether a non-Federal entity is in compliance with Y2K provisions, auditors need to consider the effect of the Y2K issue when performing tests of compliance during the audit period, particularly when the audit period includes dates after December 31, 1999.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether system/date issues could affect entity's ability to comply with award requirements or the integrity of records and adjust audit procedures accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verify institutions' responsibilities under Student Financial Assistance (SFA) programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Institutions are responsible for determining student eligibility; verifying student data (when required); calculating financial aid amounts; completing/certifying loan applications and promissory notes; drawing and disbursing SFA funds; informing borrowers of repayment responsibilities; submitting borrower data; making refunds; collecting overpayments; establishing and managing revolving loan funds; and reporting use of funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For SFA cluster audits, test institution procedures and records to ensure each institutional responsibility is performed in accordance with program rules and that third-party servicer arrangements are controlled and monitored.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title IV program procedures — SAR/ISIR and central processor handling
rubrics_metrics.description: For Title IV programs, students complete FAFS A and SARs are provided to applicants and ISIRs to institutions by the central processor; institutions use SAR/ISIR to determine eligibility, award amounts, and disbursements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify institutions properly use SAR/ISIR data, understand that the central processor is a Department service organization (SAS 70 not applicable to schools), and ensure institutional processes correctly interpret central processor outputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program-specific statutory requirements (e.g., Pell award limits and loan program terms)
rubrics_metrics.description: Programs like Pell have maximum and minimum awards established by statute; loan programs (Perkins, HPSL/PCL, NSL) have statutory programmatic features (e.g., capital contributions, matching requirements, special restrictions like PCL residency obligations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test compliance with statutory award limits, fund accounting for revolving loan funds, matching contributions, and any borrower eligibility or service obligations specific to loan programs.
